history.summary: AMBIGUITY NOTE: 'Markandeya Temple' in Maharashtra can mean two different places. This entry is the Sri Markandeya Mandir at Siddheshwar Peth (Siddheshwar Mandir Road, Modi Khana), Solapur city — the temple of the Padmashali (weaver) samaj, dedicated to Shri Markandeya Mahamuni, the sage himself, as the community's patron deity. It must NOT be confused with the ancient Markandeshwar/Markanda temple complex at Markanda, Chamorshi in Gadchiroli district, Vidarbha (a Hemadpanthi 8th–12th-century Shiva temple group on the Wainganga river, called the 'Khajuraho of Vidarbha') — a different temple several hundred km away. ALSO NOTE: despite the name, the Solapur temple's presiding figure is Sage Markandeya, not Shiva as Markandeshwar. According to a Solapur travel guide, the temple was built by the Padmashali samaj in 1893 AD (one business listing instead says establishment 1924 and '102 years in business'; the conflict is flagged). The sage Markandeya is one of the seven Chiranjeevis (immortals): tradition says he was fated to die at 16, but his devotion to Lord Shiva saved him from the messengers of death (Yama), earning him eternal youth — a story attested in the Markandeya Purana. Devotees of the temple, largely from the Padmashali weaving community, come from Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka; the annual Narali Pournima Rathotsav (chariot festival) and Markandeya Jayanti/Janmotsav are its most enthusiastic celebrations.

name: Markandeya Temple
town_description: Solapur is a major city in south-western Maharashtra, known as Siddheshwar Nagari after the 16th-century Siddheshwar Temple with the samadhi of Siddharameshwar — a city-wide pilgrimage draw. Historically a textile and bidi-manufacturing centre (famous for Solapuri chaddars), it has a central Bhui (ground) fort, a major railway junction, and is a gateway to the Pandharpur (Vitthal) pilgrimage about 70 km away.
tradition: Hinduism (Padmashali samaj community temple dedicated to Sage Markandeya)

travel.airport: Nearest major/international airport is Pune (~230–250 km, roughly 4 hours by road). Solapur's own airport has only limited domestic services (verify current connectivity before planning).
travel.railway: Solapur Junction (station code SUR), on the Mumbai–Hyderabad main line, a major railhead with trains to Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and beyond; the temple at Siddheshwar Peth is a short auto/taxi ride from the station (verify distance).
travel.road: Centrally located at Siddheshwar Peth, Modi Khana, on Siddheshwar Mandir Road, Solapur-413007; easily reached by auto-rickshaw, taxi and city bus within Solapur.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Narali Pournima (July–August, Rathotsav) and Markandeya Jayanti/Janmotsav (January–February) are the most festive times to visit, though crowded with community devotees.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily 6:00 AM to 8:45 PM, open all days (reported by two local listings; verify on site). No entry fee reported (verify); remove footwear before entering.
